Parameter estimation for PDE models

Source: R/inverse-problems.R
estimate_parameters.Rd

Estimates parameters theta of a linear elliptic model from point observations by minimizing

Usage

estimate_parameters(
  problem_fun,
  theta0,
  observations,
  mesh = NULL,
  lower = -Inf,
  upper = Inf,
  regularization = 0,
  theta_ref = theta0,
  control = list(),
  derivative = NULL
)

Arguments

problem_fun

function(theta) or function(theta, mesh) returning an elliptic_problem().

theta0

Initial parameter values.

observations

A pde_observations() object.

mesh

Optional mesh passed as second argument of problem_fun.

lower, upper

Bounds on the parameters.

regularization

Tikhonov weight lambda.

theta_ref

Reference parameters of the regularization.

control

Passed to stats::optim().

derivative

Optional exact operator derivatives, see pde_sensitivity() and affine_derivative(); indices refer to the full parameter vector.

Value

A list of class pde_estimate with the estimate, standard errors, the fixed parameters, and identifiability: one singular value per free parameter of the weighted observation sensitivity matrix (zero for directions the observations cannot see, as when there are fewer observations than free parameters), its numerical rank, the condition number (infinite when rank is below the number of free parameters), the right singular vectors directions, the null_space of unidentified parameter directions, and the correlation matrix (NULL when rank deficient). These describe the information in the data only; regularization can make the optimization well posed but adds no information.

Details

1/2 sum_i ((u_h(x_i; theta) - y_i) / sd_i)^2 + lambda/2 ||theta - theta_ref||^2

subject to the discretized PDE. The gradient is computed with the discrete adjoint method (pde_sensitivity()); the optimizer is stats::optim() with method "L-BFGS-B", so bounds are supported. Forward solves are cached so the objective and gradient at the same theta share one solve.

At the estimate, the Gauss-Newton approximation H = S^T W S + lambda I (with S the forward sensitivities of the predicted observations) gives approximate standard errors. Without regularization they are sqrt(diag(H^-1)); with lambda > 0 they are the propagated measurement noise sqrt(diag(H^-1 S^T W S H^-1)) (the regularized estimator is biased and this ignores the bias). They reflect measurement noise only, under a local linearization; they do not include discretization error. To expose the latter, the model is re-solved at the estimate on a uniformly refined mesh (when problem_fun accepts a mesh) and the change in the predicted observations is reported.

A local optimizer is used; for nonconvex problems the result is a local minimum, and no global optimality is claimed.

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8)
pf <- function(theta, mesh) poisson_problem(mesh, diffusion = theta[1], source = 1,
                                            boundary = dirichlet_bc(0))
truth <- solve_pde(pf(0.5, mesh))
xo <- c(0.3, 0.5, 0.7); yo <- c(0.5, 0.5, 0.4)
obs <- pde_observations(xo, yo, evaluate(truth$u, xo, yo), sd = 0.01)
est <- estimate_parameters(pf, theta0 = 1, observations = obs, mesh = mesh,
                           lower = 0.01)
est$estimate
#> [1] 0.5
